concerns.text: T011 mandates 'CPU-only, default precision, no 8-bit/4-bit quantization'. This directly contradicts plan.md's 'Compute Feasibility Note' which states 8-bit quantization is the ONLY way to fit models within the 7GB RAM limit. Implementing T011 as written makes the project infeasible on the target platform (GitHub Actions), violating the plan's technical solution and SC-004.

T020 implements ZINB regression as the primary test with a fallback to permutation. This contradicts plan.md 'Statistical Design' which explicitly designates the 'Permutation Test' as the primary method and ZINB as secondary/skipped if n < 128. The task weakens the specified statistical strategy, risking invalid results due to convergence failures on small samples.

T015 aggregates vulnerability counts by 'task_id' and calculates means before statistical analysis. Spec FR-004 and plan.md 'Statistical Design' define the unit of analysis as 'Individual code sample' (n=64 per group). Aggregating to task-level violates the unit of analysis, changing the statistical test from sample-level to task-level, which invalidates the comparison against SC-001.

T012 requires generating 'ALL tasks' from HumanEval and MBPP. Spec FR-002 requires 'a random set of tasks' to obtain 64 valid samples per model. Generating ALL tasks for two benchmarks across two models will likely exceed the 6-hour runtime limit (SC-004) and contradicts the 'fixed set of tasks' approach in the plan to ensure feasibility.

T023 calculates FPR but omits the explicit requirement in FR-012 to 'execute a Reference-Validator Agent on a stratified random sample of n=20 items per group' as a distinct step before calculation. While T022 handles selection, T023 lacks the logic to ensure the calculation is strictly bounded to the n=20 sample, risking calculation on the full dataset which violates FR-012.

T037a and T037b are marked as optional/rejected tasks with no implementation evidence, yet spec SC-005 defines reproducibility (identical outputs with same seed) as a mandatory success criterion. The current task list lacks a guaranteed, non-optional verification step to satisfy SC-005, creating a gap in the constraint preservation for reproducibility.
